input: In this study, flux, selectivity and stability are compared for two different membranes applied to the pervaporation separation of isopropanol from water. Pervaporation is a membrane separation process in which a liquid feed is brought into contact with one side of a membrane, whilst a vacuum maintained on the other side draws the component that permeates through the membrane in the form of a vapour. Flux is defined as the mass that permeates per unit membrane area per hour (kg m-2 h-1), and the separation factor is defined as the water-to-alcohol ratio in the permeate divided by the same ratio in the feed, which expresses how strongly the membrane enriches the permeate in water relative to the feed. A polymer membrane and a zeolite membrane were both tested using a feed consisting of 85 wt% isopropanol in water at a temperature of 60 °C. The polymer membrane was found to give a flux of 2.1 kg m-2 h-1 together with a separation factor of 120, although its flux fell by 10% over the course of 500 h. The zeolite membrane, on the other hand, gave a flux of 0.9 kg m-2 h-1 and a separation factor of 420, and its flux remained unchanged over 500 h, within the limits of measurement error. The two membranes thus divide the three measures between them: the polymer membrane permeates at the faster rate but is considerably less selective, while the zeolite membrane permeates more slowly, enriches the permeate far more strongly, and succeeded in maintaining its flux over the full duration of the test where the polymer membrane lost flux. A duty that is governed by permeate purity therefore reads rather differently from a duty that is governed by throughput, and the difference in stability is relevant to both readings, since a flux that declines during the course of a run is not the flux on which the membrane was originally selected. It should be noted that only one feed composition was tested in this work, and that no test was run beyond 500 h. Flux, selectivity and stability are seldom reported together for one and the same membrane, and the comparison is complete on those three measures for the feed tested, without extending to other compositions or longer runs.
